mainTopic: שבועת הפקדון: when one oath that denies several claims counts as one oath and when it counts as many (כלל versus פרט)
overview: The גמרא first closes an earlier discussion by saying the משנה proves nothing on that question. It then turns to the משנה of שבועת הפקדון and brings a ברייתא where four תנאים argue about when a man who falsely denies several claims in one oath is liable once (כלל) and when he is liable for each claim (פרט). שמואל and רבי יוחנן explain the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה differently, especially about the word 'and' in 'וְלֹא לָךְ'. שמואל learns his reading from the ברייתא, and רבי יוחנן learns his from the משנה. Each one answers the other's proof. Several lines of the משנה seem to go against שמואל, and the גמרא first answers by reading them without the ו. It then asks whether the תנא could really have made that mistake so many times, and says instead that the משנה follows רבי. רבי יוחנן rules that small values of several items add up to a פרוטה, and רב אחא and רבינא argue whether the general opening of the oath adds its own liability. Two counts in ברייתות of רבי חייא, fifteen and twenty, are explained so that neither one settles that argument. The amud ends with רבא asking רב נחמן about one oath said to five claimants, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No proof can be brought from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the previous discussion: nothing can be learned from this משנה on the question being asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an earlier back-and-forth. It admits that the attempt to learn something from the משנה does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא tried to draw an inference from the wording of the משנה. After the challenges, it gives up and says the משנה does not settle the question either way. The question is left open and the גמרא moves on.

keyTerms.meaning: Nothing can be learned from it

phrases.english: Rather, from this
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה the גמרא was just trying to learn from.

phrases.english: there is nothing to learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה cannot be used as a proof for the earlier question, so the question stays unresolved.

steps.title: The משנה of the oath on a deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening of the משנה that defines שבועת הפקדון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of an oath on a deposit? Someone says, "Give me the deposit of mine that is in your hand," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the משנה about שבועת הפקדון. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שבועת הפקדון, a person falsely swears that he does not have someone else's deposit. If he lied, he must bring a קרבן אשם. The כו׳ tells us the משנה goes on, including the case of several claimants, and that case is what the ברייתא will discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath denying that one holds another person's deposit
A deposit: an item left with someone for safekeeping
How so? What is the case?
Etc.; the quote continues in the source

phrases.english: What is the case of an oath on a deposit?
"Give me the deposit
of mine that is in your hand," and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after the previous discussion was closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבועת הפקדון is when a person is asked to return a deposit and swears falsely that he does not have it.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה on one oath or many
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: according to רבי מאיר, a general oath (כלל) makes him liable once and a specific oath (פרט) makes him liable for each claim. רבי יהודה says that swearing "oath, not yours and not yours and not yours" makes him liable for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If he included them all together, he is liable only once. If he specified each, he is liable for each and every one. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: "An oath, not yours, and not yours, and not yours" makes him liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a man who falsely denies several people's claims. The question is whether he brings one קרבן or one for each claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives a rule: a general denial (כלל) counts as one oath, while a specific denial (פרט) counts as many. רבי יהודה describes a concrete phrasing: the word שבועה said once at the start, with "and not yours" repeated, and he says that counts for each one. The ברייתא does not yet say exactly which phrasing רבי מאיר calls כלל and which he calls פרט.

keyTerms.meaning: A general statement that includes everyone together
A specific statement that names each one separately
Liable for each and every one (a separate קרבן for each)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he included them all together, he is liable only once.

phrases.aramaic: פְּרָט – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: If he specified each one, he is liable for each and every one.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: ״שְׁבוּעָה לֹא לְךָ וְלֹא לְךָ וְלֹא לָךְ״ –
phrases.english: "An oath, nothing of yours, and nothing of yours, and nothing of yours"
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּלָל – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's case of an oath to several claimants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: כלל means liable once and פרט means liable for each. רבי יהודה: "oath, not yours and not yours and not yours" means liable for each.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון add their views
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי אליעזר says liability for each claim happens when the word שבועה comes at the end. רבי שמעון says it only happens if he says שבועה separately to each person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: "Not yours, and not yours, and not yours, an oath" makes him liable for each and every one. רבי שמעון says: Not until he says "oath" to each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא brings two more opinions on what wording makes a person liable separately for each claimant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר moves the word שבועה to the end. Then it seems to apply back to each denial, so he is liable for each. רבי שמעון is the strictest about wording: each denial needs its own word שבועה before it counts as a separate oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Not until he says; only if he says

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא לְךָ וְלֹא לְךָ וְלֹא לְךָ, שְׁבוּעָה״ –
phrases.english: "Nothing of yours, and nothing of yours, and nothing of yours, on my oath"
he is liable for each and every one.
Rabbi Shimon says:
He is not liable for each until he says "oath"
to each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with additional opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: if שבועה is said at the end, he is liable for each. רבי שמעון: he is liable for each only if he says שבועה to each one.
steps.whatToRemember: Four תנאים argue about wording: רבי מאיר speaks of כלל and פרט, רבי יהודה puts שבועה at the start, רבי אליעזר puts it at the end, and רבי שמעון requires שבועה for each person.

steps.title: שמואל: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה use the terms in opposite ways
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that the phrasing רבי מאיר calls כלל, רבי יהודה calls פרט, and the reverse is also true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי מאיר's general case is רבי יהודה's specific case, and רבי יהודה's general case is רבי מאיר's specific case.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains what the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה really is. They disagree about which wording counts as general and which counts as specific.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wording with "and" between the denials ("not yours AND not yours") is a כלל to רבי מאיר but a פרט to רבי יהודה. Wording without "and" ("not yours, not yours") is a כלל to רבי יהודה but a פרט to רבי מאיר. So they agree on the rule (כלל = once, פרט = each) and only argue about which wording fits each label.

keyTerms.meaning: His general case: what he considers a כלל
His specific case: what he considers a פרט
רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume כלל means the same wording for both תנאים. The same sentence is a כלל to one and a פרט to the other, so always ask whose כלל you are talking about.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the whole ברייתא. The argument is not about the rule itself. It is about how to understand the word "and": does it join the denials together, or does it split them apart?

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The general case of Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: This is the wording with "and" between the denials: "not yours and not yours."

phrases.english: is the specific case of Rabbi Yehuda;
the general case of Rabbi Yehuda
phrases.notes: This is the wording without "and": "not yours, not yours, not yours."

phrases.english: is the specific case of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּלָלוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the terms כלל and פרט in the ברייתא's argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With "and": כלל for רבי מאיר and פרט for רבי יהודה. Without "and": כלל for רבי יהודה and פרט for רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's different reading of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says everyone agrees that "וְלֹא לָךְ" is פרט. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about "לֹא לָךְ". For רבי מאיר, the כלל case is "שבועה שאין לכם בידי", which uses the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: Everyone agrees that "and not yours" is specific. They argue only about "not yours": רבי מאיר says it is specific, and רבי יהודה says it is general. So what does רבי מאיר count as general? "An oath that I have nothing of yours (all of you)."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second explanation of the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, and it is different from שמואל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, adding the word "and" (וְלֹא לָךְ) makes it פרט even for רבי מאיר, and רבי יהודה says so outright. The two תנאים argue only when the "and" is missing. For רבי מאיר, only one sentence spoken to everyone together in the plural, "שאין לכם", counts as כלל.

keyTerms.meaning: "And not yours" (each person named, with the word "and")
"To you" in the plural, all of you together

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two wordings. "וְלֹא לָךְ" has the extra "and"; "לֹא לָךְ" does not. According to רבי יוחנן, the whole argument is about that one small letter ו.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּ״וְלֹא לָךְ״ – שֶׁהוּא פְּרָט;
phrases.english: Everyone agrees about "and not yours" that it is specific;
phrases.notes: "Specific" means he is liable separately for each person he swore to.

phrases.english: they only argued about "not yours"
that Rabbi Meir says it is specific,
and Rabbi Yehuda says it is general.
And what is Rabbi Meir's general case?
"An oath that I have nothing of yours (all of you)."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation from שמואל's in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "וְלֹא לָךְ" is פרט according to everyone. With "לֹא לָךְ", רבי מאיר says פרט and רבי יהודה says כלל. For רבי מאיר, כלל is only "שבועה שאין לכם בידי".

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל and רבי יוחנן explain רבי מאיר in such different ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what makes שמואל and רבי יוחנן read the dispute differently. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים are explaining the same ברייתא. The גמרא wants to know what source or reasoning pushes each one to his own reading.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means שמואל and רבי יוחנן, not רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the two readings in steps 5 and 6 are different
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source each אמורא relies on for his reading

steps.title: One learns from the ברייתא, the other from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל draws his reading out of the ברייתא. רבי יוחנן draws his out of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל inferred from the ברייתא, and רבי יוחנן inferred from the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in short form: each אמורא is working from a different text. It will explain each one next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is not just about logic. Each one is reading closely from a different source. שמואל looks at how רבי יהודה reacts in the ברייתא. רבי יוחנן looks at which example the משנה chose to give.

keyTerms.meaning: Reads closely and draws a conclusion from the wording
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Shmuel inferred from the baraita,
and Rabbi Yochanan inferred from the mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל relies on the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן relies on the משנה

steps.title: שמואל's proof from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says "וְלֹא לָךְ" is פרט. That suggests רבי מאיר said it was כלל, and רבי יהודה was arguing with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל inferred from the ברייתא: רבי יהודה says "and not yours" is specific. We can infer that he heard רבי מאיר say it is general, and רבי יהודה answered him: it is specific.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how שמואל reads the ברייתא to support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנא usually speaks up to disagree. So when רבי יהודה says "וְלֹא לָךְ" is פרט, it shows that רבי מאיר held the opposite, that it is כלל. This is the basis for שמואל's "reverse" reading.

keyTerms.meaning: We can infer from this that

phrases.english: Shmuel inferred from the baraita:

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה ״וְלֹא לָךְ״ פְּרָטָא הָוֵי –
phrases.english: since Rabbi Yehuda says "and not yours" is specific,
we infer that he heard Rabbi Meir
say it is general,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: פְּרָטָא הָוֵי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda said to him: it is specific.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל דָּיֵיק מִבָּרַיְיתָא: מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out שמואל's side of the answer in step 8
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that רבי מאיר holds "וְלֹא לָךְ" is כלל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement in the ברייתא that "וְלֹא לָךְ" is פרט

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר holds that both wordings are פרט. רבי יהודה agrees about "וְלֹא לָךְ" and disagrees only about "לֹא לָךְ".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: רבי מאיר holds both are specific. רבי יהודה said to him: about "and not yours" I agree with you; about "not yours" I disagree with you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back on שמואל's proof by showing that the ברייתא can be read another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe רבי יהודה mentions "וְלֹא לָךְ" only to say where he agrees. Then the ברייתא does not prove that רבי מאיר called it כלל. That takes away שמואל's proof.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
according to Rabbi Meir, both are specific;
and Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
about "and not yours" I agree with you,
about "not yours" I disagree with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר פְּרָטָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects שמואל's proof in step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא, not שמואל's view itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's statement may be telling us where he agrees, not answering an opposite view

steps.title: שמואל's objection: why mention where he agrees?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers: if that were true, רבי יהודה should have stated the case where he disagrees, not the case where he agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל would say: instead of agreeing with him, let him disagree with him!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends his proof. He asks why רבי יהודה would bother to say where he agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a dispute, the speaker normally states his disagreement. If רבי יהודה really argued only about "לֹא לָךְ", he should have said that. Since he mentions "וְלֹא לָךְ", that must be the case they argue about.

phrases.english: And Shmuel would say:
instead of agreeing with him,
let him disagree with him!
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה should have named the case where they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל's reply to רבי יוחנן's rejection in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא states the point where he disagrees, not the point where he agrees

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives "שבועה שאין לכם בידי" as its example of כלל. If "וְלֹא לָךְ" were also כלל, the משנה would have given that bolder example instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן inferred from the משנה: רבי מאיר says "an oath that I have nothing of yours (plural)" is general. That implies "and not yours" is specific. Because if you think "and not yours" is general, then instead of teaching us the plural case, the משנה should teach "an oath, not yours and not yours and not yours" is general. We would then know all the more so about the plural case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן proves his view from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teacher gives the biggest example, so the easier one is understood without being said. The משנה picked the obvious plural case as its כלל. That shows the bigger case, "וְלֹא לָךְ", is not כלל for רבי מאיר. So it must be פרט.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: in the ברייתא, רבי יהודה is answering רבי מאיר, so רבי מאיר called "וְלֹא לָךְ" כלל. רבי יוחנן: the משנה chose the plural "לכם" as its כלל example, so "וְלֹא לָךְ" must be פרט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא reads a משנה: it assumes the משנה chose the strongest example. So the example it picked tells us where the line really falls.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan inferred from the mishnah:
since Rabbi Meir says:
phrases.notes: The unnamed voice of the משנה is treated here as רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: "an oath that I have nothing of yours (plural)" is general,
we infer that "and not yours" is specific;
for if it would enter your mind
that "and not yours" is general,
then instead of teaching us "an oath that I have nothing of yours (plural)",

phrases.aramaic: נַשְׁמְעִינַן ״שְׁבוּעָה לֹא לָךְ וְלֹא לָךְ וְלֹא לָךְ״,
phrases.english: let it teach us "an oath, not yours and not yours and not yours" is general,
and all the more so "an oath that I have nothing of yours (plural)"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 8 and explains רבי יוחנן's side
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that "וְלֹא לָךְ" is פרט even for רבי מאיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's choice of "שבועה שאין לכם בידי" as its example of כלל

steps.title: שמואל deflects רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that adding "וְלֹא לָךְ" is like saying one general oath, "I have nothing of yours."
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Anyone who says "and not yours" is treated like someone who says "an oath that I have nothing of yours (all of you) in my hand."
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה. He says the משנה's example 'שבועה שאין לכם בידי' also includes someone who says 'וְלֹא לָךְ', so the משנה proves nothing against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן argued that the משנה would have taught the bigger case, 'וְלֹא לָךְ', if that were also a כלל. שמואל answers that 'וְלֹא לָךְ' is the same as the plural 'לכם'. The ו joins the denials into one, so the משנה's example covers both cases, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: "And not yours": the wording with the connecting ו
"An oath that I have nothing of yours": a general denial (כלל)
A general statement that counts as one oath

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Anyone who says "and not yours"
is like one who says "an oath that I have nothing of yours in my hand."
phrases.notes: "לָכֶם" is plural, "of all of you." That makes it one sweeping denial instead of separate ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל's rebuttal of רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה in step 12; the גמרא then tests שמואל against other lines of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "וְלֹא לָךְ" with a ו counts as a single general oath (כלל).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה's choice of example
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'וְלֹא לָךְ' is equal to 'שאין לכם', so the משנה's plural example already covers it and did not need a separate case.

steps.title: Challenge from the triple "and not yours" in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says "not yours, and not yours, and not yours," and counts each one as a separate oath. That goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: "Not yours, and not yours, and not yours!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה, where the words are joined by "and" and the person is still liable for each oath separately. This seems to disprove שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "וְלֹא לָךְ" were a כלל like שמואל says, the משנה should give only one oath here. Instead the משנה counts each phrase as its own oath, so the ו did not join them into one.

keyTerms.meaning: A specific statement; each one is its own oath

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: ״לֹא לָךְ וְלֹא לָךְ וְלֹא לָךְ״!
phrases.english: We learned: "Not yours, and not yours, and not yours!"
phrases.notes: In the משנה, someone who says this is liable for each one. That is the problem for שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's statement from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that "וְלֹא לָךְ" is a כלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה uses "וְלֹא לָךְ" and still counts separate oaths, so it treats the wording as a פרט.

steps.title: Read the משנה without the "and"
steps.stepSummary: Answer: change the wording of the משנה to "not yours, not yours, not yours," with no ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: "Not yours" (not yours, not yours), without the "and."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the משנה should be read without the connecting ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ו, each "לֹא לָךְ" stands alone, and according to שמואל that wording is a פרט for רבי מאיר, whose view the משנה follows. Now the משנה no longer speaks about "וְלֹא לָךְ", and שמואל's view stands.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the law is different. It is only changing which wording the משנה used, so the case fits שמואל.

phrases.english: Teach: "Not yours."
phrases.notes: Read the whole list this way: "not yours, not yours, not yours," with no "and."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה uses "וְלֹא לָךְ" and counts separate oaths.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה really says "לֹא לָךְ" with no ו, which according to שמואל is a פרט for רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Challenge from the deposit, pledge, stolen and lost items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists "a deposit, and a pledge, and a stolen item, and a lost item," joined by "and," and counts each separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "Give me the deposit, and the pledge, and the stolen item, and the lost item!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case from the משנה where items joined by "and" are each counted as a separate oath. This again seems to go against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list uses the ו again. Since the משנה makes the person liable for each item, the "and" did not make the denial one general oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Something handed over, like a loan or pledge
A stolen item and a lost item

phrases.english: Come and hear: "Give me the deposit
and the pledge, and the stolen item, and the lost item!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against שמואל, built the same way as step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the connecting ו makes a כלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items joined by ו are counted separately in the משנה, so the ו makes a פרט.

steps.title: Read the list without the "and"
steps.stepSummary: Answer: read the list as "pledge, stolen item, lost item," with no ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: "Pledge, stolen item, lost item."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer: the list in the משנה had no connecting ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ו, each item is a separate denial, a פרט, so separate oaths make sense. שמואל's view is not hurt.

phrases.english: Teach: "Pledge, stolen item, lost item."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list is joined with ו and still counted separately.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list has no ו, so each item is a פרט.

steps.title: Challenge from the wheat, barley and spelt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says "Give me wheat, and barley, and spelt," joined by "and," and counts each separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "Give me wheat, and barley, and spelt!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third case from the משנה with the same problem for שמואל: items joined by "and" that are counted separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the ו appears, and the משנה makes him liable for each grain. That suggests the ו creates a פרט, against שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״תֵּן לִי חִטִּין וּשְׂעוֹרִין וְכוּסְּמִין״!
phrases.english: Come and hear: "Give me wheat, and barley, and spelt!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against שמואל, built like steps 14 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the connecting ו makes a כלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The grains are joined by ו and counted separately, so the ו makes a פרט.

steps.title: Read the grains without the "and"
steps.stepSummary: Answer: read it as "barley, spelt," with no ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: "Barley, spelt."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third challenge the same way: the משנה had no connecting ו in this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no ו, each grain is a separate denial, a פרט, so separate oaths fit. All three challenges are answered with one method, and שמואל's view survives.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל says "וְלֹא לָךְ" is one general oath, a כלל. Every time the משנה seems to count "and" items separately, the גמרא answers "תְּנִי": read the משנה without the ו.

phrases.english: Teach: "Barley, spelt."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and closes the run of challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grains are joined with ו and counted separately.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list has no ו, so each grain is a פרט, and שמואל stands.

steps.title: Could the Teacher of the משנה Really Err So Many Times?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to its own approach of removing the ו from the משנה again and again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it be that this תנא kept making mistakes in so many places as he taught?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at all the times it deleted the letter ו from the משנה and asks whether that can really be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 15, 17 and 19 the גמרא fixed the משנה by taking out the ו each time. Doing that once is acceptable, but doing it over and over suggests the whole approach is wrong. This pushes the גמרא to look for a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage who taught the משנה

phrases.english: And this teacher of the Mishnah, so much
makes mistakes as he goes on teaching?!
phrases.notes: This is about all the earlier answers that removed the ו from the משנה over and over.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי תַּנָּא כֹּל הָכִי שָׁבֵישׁ תָּנֵי וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the whole series of 'remove the ו' answers given in steps 15, 17, 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The approach of fixing the משנה by deleting the ו each time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is not reasonable that a תנא made the same wording mistake so many times in one משנה.

steps.title: The משנה Follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: the משנה follows רבי, for whom a list counts item by item whether or not it has a ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whose view is this משנה? It is רבי, who says: whether one says 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk' or 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk', either way each item counts separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea of fixing the wording and says the משנה follows רבי instead of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the ו makes no difference, because both ways of listing count each item on its own. So the משנה's lists with ו are fine as written and nothing needs to be removed. The problem only came up because the משנה was being read according to רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A detailed listing, where each item counts separately

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole approach: rather than fixing the wording, the גמרא changes which תנא the משנה follows.

phrases.english: Rather, whose view is this? It is Rabbi,
who says: there is no difference if one says 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk',
and there is no difference if one says 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk' —
either way it is a detailed listing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by giving up the wording fixes and assigning the משנה to רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which תנא the משנה follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, so the ו had to be removed again and again.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי, for whom a list with or without ו counts each item, so the text stays as it is.

steps.title: A Challenge from רבי מאיר's Own Words
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה, רבי מאיר himself uses a list with ו and still counts each item separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear from his own words: רבי מאיר says, even if he said 'a grain of wheat and barley and spelt,' he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי מאיר's own statement in the משנה to challenge the view that for him a list with ו does not count item by item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's line in the משנה joins the grains with ו, yet he rules that the person is liable for each one. That seems to show that for רבי מאיר the ו does not join the items into one. This goes against the way his view was explained earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable for each and every one

phrases.english: Come and hear from his own words:
Rabbi Meir says,
even if he said 'a grain of wheat and a grain of barley and a grain of spelt' —
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to how רבי מאיר's view was explained and tests it against his own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation that, for רבי מאיר, only a list without ו counts each item separately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר himself uses ו and still makes him liable for each item.

steps.title: Read רבי מאיר's Words Without the ו
steps.stepSummary: The answer: read רבי מאיר's line as 'wheat, barley, spelt' with no ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'a grain of wheat, a grain of barley, a grain of spelt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by taking the ו out of רבי מאיר's line, just as it did before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ו, the list is clearly a detailed listing even for רבי מאיר, so liability for each item fits his view. The challenge from step 22 goes away.

phrases.english: Teach: 'a grain of wheat, a grain of barley, a grain of spelt.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's line has ו, so it seems he counts each item even with ו.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's line has no ו, so it fits his view.

steps.title: What Does 'Even' Add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point רבי מאיר is making with the word 'even.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי מאיר's wording and sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' (אפילו) suggests a surprising case. But once the ו is removed, the list is plainly detailed, so it is not clear what is surprising here.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, which points to a surprising case

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'even'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the line that was just explained in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What surprising case רבי מאיר's 'even' is meant to include

steps.title: A Single Grain Includes All of That Grain
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא explains: even though he says 'a grain' in the singular, he means all of that kind of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רב איקא said: even though he said 'a grain of wheat,' that includes all wheat; 'a grain of barley' includes all barley; and 'a grain of spelt' includes all spelt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers the question by explaining what the 'even' adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprise is in the singular words. You might think 'a grain of wheat' means only one tiny grain. רבי מאיר teaches that it still covers all the wheat being claimed, so the oath is a real denial of each kind of grain.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי, for whom both kinds of lists count item by item. רבי מאיר's line is read without ו, and his 'even' teaches that a singular word like 'a grain of wheat' covers all the wheat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said:
even 'a grain of wheat' includes all wheat,
and 'a grain of barley' includes all barley,
and 'a grain of spelt' includes all spelt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: אֲפִילּוּ חִטָּה בִּכְלַל חִטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Even' teaches that a singular word like 'a grain of wheat' still covers all of that kind of grain.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Deposit, Pledge, Stolen and Lost Items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the משנה's case of 'give me my deposit, pledge, stolen item and lost item.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Give me the deposit, and the pledge, the stolen item and the lost item that I have in your hands,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line of the משנה. This sets up the next statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new ruling is given here yet. The quote marks the place in the משנה that the next discussion will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit, an item left with someone to watch
A pledge or a loan given into someone's hand

phrases.english: 'Give me the deposit and the pledge,

phrases.aramaic: גָּזֵל וַאֲבֵידָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי בְּיָדְךָ״ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: the stolen item and the lost item that I have in your hands,' etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּן לִי פִּקָּדוֹן וּתְשׂוּמֶת יָד גָּזֵל וַאֲבֵידָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי בְּיָדְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the ו discussion to a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's case of one claim that lists several items.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Values Add Up to a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of 'give me wheat and barley,' רבי יוחנן rules that the values of all the items together can make up the פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Give me wheat and barley': רבי יוחנן said: a פרוטה's worth from all of them together counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's ruling on the משנה's case of a claim for several kinds of grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if each kind of grain alone is worth less than a פרוטה, their values join together. If the total reaches a פרוטה, the oath makes him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin, the minimum value that counts

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן does not say each grain must be worth a פרוטה. He says the values of all the grains together can add up to one פרוטה.

phrases.english: 'Give me wheat and barley' —
phrases.notes: This is the case from the משנה that we saw in step 18.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
a peruta's worth from all of them combines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פְּרוּטָה מִכּוּלָּם מִצְטָרֶפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an אמורא's ruling on the case in the משנה section just opened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The values of all the claimed items combine to reach the minimum of a פרוטה.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא argue about the general oath
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says he is liable only for the specific items. The other says the opening general oath also makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One says: he is liable for the specific items, but not for the general oath. The other says: he is liable for the general oath too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between two אמוראים about the משנה's case where a man swore he did not have someone's wheat, barley and spelt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath has two parts. There is a general opening, 'I swear you have nothing of yours in my hands.' Then come specific items, 'wheat, barley, spelt.' Both sides agree each specific item brings a separate קרבן. They argue only about whether the general opening also counts as its own קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The specific items named one by one
The general statement that covers everything
He is liable (here, to bring a קרבן)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree he is liable for each specific item. The only argument is whether the general opening adds one more קרבן.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה's ruling that he is liable for each item: wheat, barley and spelt.

phrases.english: One says:
He is liable for the specific items,
but he is not liable for the general one.
phrases.notes: The 'general one' is the opening line: 'I swear you have nothing of yours in my hands.'

phrases.english: And one says:
He is liable for the general one too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues discussing the משנה's 'wheat, barley and spelt' case that רבי יוחנן addressed in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: he is liable only for the specific items. Other view: he is also liable for the general oath.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי חייא's count of fifteen
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא counted fifteen חטאות, not twenty. That fits only the view that the general oath does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא teach: 'Here there are fifteen sin-offerings'? If the general oath counted, there would be twenty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second opinion, which says the general oath also counts, using a ברייתא of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חייא's case, five people each claimed wheat, barley and spelt. Five claimants times three items gives fifteen. If each claimant's general oath also counted, it would be five times four, which is twenty. So the number fifteen seems to show the general oath does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (introduces a ברייתא as a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't רבי חייא teach:
'Here there are fifteen sin-offerings'?
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the general oath also counts.

phrases.english: there would be twenty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second opinion in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that he is liable for the general oath too.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's total of fifteen matches only the specific items. With the general oaths added, the total would be twenty.

steps.title: רבי חייא counted only the specific items
steps.stepSummary: The תנא chose to count only the specific oaths. He left the general oaths out of his count.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא counts the specific ones. He does not count the general ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי חייא's number did not include everything; it counted only one type of oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fifteen does not prove the general oath carries no liability. רבי חייא was simply counting the specific oaths. So the second opinion still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: This תנא
counts the specific ones;
he does not count the general ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source: the count was partial.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought fifteen was the full total of all his liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fifteen counts only the specific oaths, so the general oath may still carry liability.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי חייא's count of twenty
steps.stepSummary: A different teaching of רבי חייא says twenty חטאות. That seems to include the general oaths, which goes against the first opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא did teach: 'Here there are twenty sin-offerings'!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns around and attacks the first opinion, which says the general oath does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty is exactly five claimants times four oaths: three specific ones plus one general. So it looks like רבי חייא does count the general oath. That would go against the first opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introduces a ברייתא as a challenge)

phrases.english: But רבי חייא did teach:
'Here there are twenty sin-offerings'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 28 and challenges the first opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that he is not liable for the general oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Twenty equals five times (three specific oaths plus one general), so it seems the general oath was counted.

steps.title: The twenty is about four different items
steps.stepSummary: The 'twenty' teaching is about a different case: each claimant claimed four items. Four times five is twenty, with no general oaths counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: That teaching is about a deposit, a pledge, a stolen item and a lost item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The 'twenty' comes from a case with four specific items, not three grains plus a general oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the five claimants claimed four things: פקדון, תשומת יד, גזל and אבידה. That gives twenty specific oaths. So this count also includes no general oaths, and the first opinion still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A pledge, or money handed over (like a loan or partnership)
A lost item that was found

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רבי חייא's numbers count only specific oaths. Fifteen = 5 × 3 grains; twenty = 5 × 4 items. So neither ברייתא settles the argument between רב אחא and רבינא.

phrases.english: That one is about a deposit and a pledge
and a stolen item and a lost item.
phrases.notes: Four items for each of five people: 4 × 5 = 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אַפִּקָּדוֹן וּתְשׂוּמֶת יָד וְגָזֵל וַאֲבֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the case the source is about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought twenty meant three grains plus one general oath for each claimant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Twenty means four separate claimed items for each of five claimants, all specific oaths.

steps.title: רבא asks about one oath covering five claimants
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן about a man who swears in full to one claimant and adds 'and not yours' four times. Is he liable for only one oath for each of those four claimants?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: Five people were suing a man. They said to him, 'Give us the deposit, pledge, stolen item and lost item of ours that you have.' He said to one of them, 'I swear that you do not have a deposit, pledge, stolen item or lost item in my hands. And not yours, and not yours, and not yours, and not yours.' What is the law? Is he liable for only one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. רבא asks רב נחמן how to count the oaths when one claimant gets the full list and the other four only get 'and not yours.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: To the first claimant he named all four items. To the other four he only said 'and not yours.' רבא wants to know whether each short 'and not yours' counts as just one oath, or as four, one for each item it refers back to. The question continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question of law)

phrases.english: רבא asked רב נחמן:
If five people were suing him,
and they said to him: 'Give us the deposit,
pledge, and stolen item and lost item
of ours that are in your hands';
he said to one of them:
'I swear that you do not have in my hands a deposit,
pledge, stolen item or lost item,
and not yours, and not yours,
and not yours, and not yours' —
what is the law?
Is he liable for just one,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case of five claimants with four items (step 32) and asks a new question about the short 'and not yours' wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether each 'and not yours' counts as one oath, or as a separate oath for each of the four items it refers to.
